subject: Post-call: NeuralFleet streaming gating & GPU slate
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: NeuralFleet streaming gating & GPU slate

Hi Priya — thanks for the time today. Short recap and clear asks so we can move to a focused pilot kickoff.

Call highlights:
- Goal: Meet interactive streaming SLOs for agent UI and webhook-backed inference (low token-latency while supporting long-context streaming).
- Primary SLAs discussed: p50 ~40ms, p95 <=90ms, p99 <=140ms for 256-token streaming window (end-to-end, application measured).
- Expected steady-state concurrent sessions: ~70–100 active streams during peak, average request size ~120 tokens, occasional bursts to 300 tokens.
- Target reserved throughput: baseline to cover 80 concurrent streams with headroom (~40M tokens/day).

Constraints / notes from the call:
- NeuralFleet needs customer data to remain in their VPC for the pilot (Private deployment).
- They use a mix of short interactive prompts + multi-turn streaming; prefix reuse rate expected to be ~35% due to shared system prompts.
- Hard procurement window: vendor selection decision by 2026-11-05.

Immediate asks from Redwood (to move to sizing/pilot):
1) Tokenized sample traces (2–3 representative sessions, include avg token-length, burst patterns).
2) Confirmation of peak concurrent streams and whether bursts are abrupt or ramped.
3) Any packet inspection/IDS constraints we should consider for Private deployment network egress.

Proposed validation path (we'll run this as part of the reserved-capacity pilot):
- Microbenchmark matrix comparing A100-80GB vs H100-80GB quantized runtimes across streaming path (KV cache warm vs cold), 3 sequence profiles (short/med/long), and concurrency sweep (20/50/100).
- 48-hour soak of the selected config at 80 concurrent streams to validate p99 and tail behavior.
- Metrics we will surface: per-token latency distribution, tail stalls (cache miss tail), end-to-end streaming time-to-first-token, and GPU utilization / memory headroom.

I attached a preliminary perf_matrix_20261007.xlsx with the proposed test cells.

Next steps / owners:
- Priya: send token traces and confirm concurrency burst pattern by Fri 2026-10-09.
- Marissa: IAR (internal architect review) to validate network constraints — you own.
- Karthik: prepare the microbench-runbook.md and allocate dev-time for the 48-hour soak (target calendar week 2026-10-19).

If that aligns, I'll lock in the kickoff window and start provisioning a Private test cluster using a short-lived VPC deployment.

Thanks — Lukas

Thanks Lukas — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifications.

1) Token traces: attaching two anonymized session traces (short-session.json, long-session.json) — see Drive folder. They reflect production behavior; short sessions ~80 tokens, long ~260 tokens. Burst behavior is abrupt — we see sudden fanout when our webhooks fan triggers across endpoints.

2) Peak concurrency: confirmed peak observed is 95 active streams in the US region; sustained at 70+ for several hours.

3) Network: we use an internal appliance for IDS; we need TLS passthrough. No deep packet inspection on the content payloads.

Procurement note: our procurement lead prefers an initial 30-day pilot with SLA gating; procurement will likely ask for a 6-8 week POC to evaluate stability. Decision timeline (internal): vendor short-list by 2026-11-01, final by 2026-11-18.

Subject: Re: Post-call: NeuralFleet streaming gating & GPU slate (tech prep)

Quick tech notes after reviewing the perf matrix and Priya's trace notes:

- GPU tradeoffs: H100 (FP8/quant) gives better throughput for heavy batching but historically shows slightly higher first-token tail in streaming due to kernel scheduling when KV cache grows. A100 (FP16) is often better for deterministic tail and TTF token under 150ms when sequence lengths are <=320 and KV cache fits within 40–60GB. Since they have abrupt bursts and many short sessions, A100-80 may be a safer initial pick for p99 targets.

- Caching: with ~35% prefix reuse, enabling prefix-KV caching will drop per-token work substantially; we should include warm/cold cache cells in the matrix. Also measure time-to-first-token on warm cache (expected ~20–35ms p50).

- Concurrency sizing: propose we size pilot cluster for 120 concurrent streams ( ~25% headroom above observed peak). This gives safety for spikes and simplifies SLO validation.

- Tests I will prepare (microbench-runbook.md attached):
  * Kernel latency sweep (1–512 tokens)
  * Concurrency ramp test (20 -> 120 over 20m)
  * Soak: 48h at 80 concurrent, then 24h at 110 to stress tail behavior
- Measurement hooks: time-to-first-byte, time-to-first-token, per-token P99, GPU power/thermals, and queueing latency on the serving tier.

I'll stage the runbook and coordinate with infra for the Private VPC images. If we pick A100 initially, we can still run an H100 check for per-token throughput comparisons during the soak (one-off).

—Karthik
